english.title: Remain unlawfully at large after expiry of release period under intermittent custody order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been temporarily released on **(..SPECIFY THE RELEASE DATE..) from **(..SPECIFY THE ESTABLISHMENT FROM WHICH RELEASED..) in pursuance of an intermittent custody order made under section 183 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, without reasonable excuse you remained unlawfully at large after becoming so at large by virtue of the expiry of the period for which you were temporarily released
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1A) and (3) of the Prisoners (Return to Custody) Act 1995.

english.notes:
(i) Section 1(1A) of the Prisoners (Return to Custody) Act 1995 was inserted by section 186(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003.
(ii) Section 1(4) provides that an offence under this section shall be taken to be committed at the place where the offender was required to be detained immediately before being temporarily released.
(iii) section 1(5) provides that a person shall be deemed for the purposes of this section to be unlawfully at large whenever he is deemed to be so at large for the purposes of section 49 of the Prison Act 1952 (which confers powers of arrest).

other.powersofarrest: Arrest without warrantSection 49(1) of the Prison Act 1952 provides that any person who, having been sentenced to imprisonment, custody for life or youth custody or ordered to be detained in a detention centre or young offenders institution or a secure training centre, or having been committed to a prison or remand centre, is unlawfully at large, may be arrested by a constable without warrant and taken to the place in which he is required in accordance with law to be detained.
